core_obligations: Reduce to the affine case: by restriction of differentials to opens one may assume X = Spec(A) and S = Spec(R), so the task becomes the comparison between the module of global sections of the sheaf of differentials with its derivation and the algebra module of differentials of the ring map (proof lines 6668-6672).

Set up the two comparison arrows: for an A-module N with associated quasi-coherent sheaf, precomposing by the derivation d of global sections gives a map alpha from A-linear maps of the module of global sections into N to the R-derivations of A into N, and combining the identifications of derivations of sheaves and of modules with taking global sections gives the reverse arrow beta (proof lines 6673-6697).

Check that alpha and beta are inverse to one another by testing on global sections, conclude that the module of global sections together with its derivation satisfies the universal property of the module of differentials of the ring map, and apply Yoneda's lemma to get the unique compatible isomorphism (proof lines 6698-6702).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to affine source and target and compare two functors of the module of differentials by explicit arrows (proof lines 6668-6697).
Show the arrows are mutually inverse and conclude by the universal property and Yoneda's lemma (proof lines 6698-6702).
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the module of global sections of the sheaf of relative differentials over an affine chart with the algebra module of differentials of the corresponding ring map, compatibly with the two derivations (statement lines 6657-6666). The counted proof reduces to the affine case by restriction of differentials and then compares two representable functors through two explicitly written arrows, alpha from the linear maps of the module of global sections to the derivations and beta constructed from the identifications of sheaf derivations and module derivations, checks that they are mutually inverse on global sections, and concludes by the universal property together with Yoneda's lemma (proof lines 6668-6702). It is H2: the argument is a complete functorial comparison carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being the universal property and Yoneda's lemma.
